# Weighted legacy-description fixture

Generated by `tests/fixtures/generate_weighted.py` using only Python's standard
library. The 315-byte source protobuf uses Core ML specification version 9,
CoreML7 MIL operations, and legacy ModelDescription input/output fields rather
than function descriptions. It contains a ranged `[?, 4]` input and an `add`
with four external FP32 weights `[2, -3, 5, -7]`.

The 192-byte version-2 weight file contains one entry. Its metadata starts at
offset 64; the four little-endian floats start at offset 128. This fixture is
synthetic and contains no community-model data or downloaded assets.

## Native golden capture

Captured on 2026-09-25 with Xcode 27.0 (27A266a), coremlc 3600.25.1,
MIL component 3600.16.1. The checked-in `expected-macos.mlmodelc` is unmodified
Apple compiler output, not output from this crate. Capture used:

```sh
python3 tests/fixtures/generate_weighted.py --check
capture_dir=$(mktemp -d)
xcrun coremlc compile tests/fixtures/flexible-weighted-legacy/input.mlmodel "$capture_dir"
```

The resulting `input.mlmodelc` was copied to `expected-macos.mlmodelc`.
Compilation and golden comparison do not establish runtime correctness on the
capture host or any device. CI separately runs exact predictions on macOS 15;
physical iOS/watchOS execution remains a distinct validation step.

## Independent value check

`tests/runtime_shapes.swift` loads a freshly Rust-compiled bundle with CPU-only
compute units and runs row counts `1 -> 2 -> 4 -> 1` on the same model. Input
element `i` is `i - 8`; expected output is `i - 8 + [2, -3, 5, -7][i % 4]`.
It checks every shape and all 32 values exactly using coordinate-aware access.
Expected values do not come from either compiler's output.
